sub_goals.text: Hospital orders recorded accurately and confirmed promptly
kpis: Order lines matching the hospital purchase order
>= 99.5% per month
Order confirmation sent after submission
within 15 minutes
beliefs: Each hospital has a contract price list
Hospital buyers order through the portal or the assistant
constraints: A confirmed order cannot be changed without a change request

elements.text: Capture the hospital purchase order in the order portal with automatic validation of each line against the hospital contract price list and contract catalogue
Send the order confirmation to the hospital buyer automatically at order submission, before batch, lot and expiry checks are performed at picking
Route any change to a confirmed order through a recorded change request and re-issue a new confirmation to the hospital buyer
Log the submission and confirmation timestamp of every order and report monthly on confirmation delay and line-matching deviations
Hospital contract price list and contract catalogue
Order management module with hospital ordering portal
LLM ordering assistant with retrieval restricted to the approved hospital contract catalogue
Order confirmation and change-request log
Hospital Buyer
Sales Administrator
Each hospital has a contract price list, so order lines must be priced and validated per hospital
Hospital buyers order through the portal or the LLM assistant, so both channels must produce the same recorded and confirmable order
A confirmed order cannot be changed without a recorded change request
An order line that is not on the hospital contract catalogue is held for the Sales Administrator instead of being confirmed

sub_goals.text: Batch and expiry traceable to each hospital
kpis: Shipped lines with batch number and expiry date recorded
Time to list every hospital that received a recalled batch
under 2 hours
beliefs: Good distribution practice requires batch records for every medicine
constraints: A line without batch and expiry cannot be shipped

elements.text: Scan and record batch number and expiry date at goods receipt of each pharmaceutical pack
Record batch number and expiry date on each picked order line at picking, after order confirmation
Suggest picking by earliest expiry (FEFO) and block confirmation of a shipped line that has no batch number or expiry date
Report batches expiring within 90 days and remove expired stock from sellable inventory
Run a recall trace report that lists every hospital, delivery note and quantity for a given batch number
Quarantine stock of a recalled or suspect batch and notify the affected Hospital Buyers pending the release decision

sub_goals.text: Cold-chain products kept within their temperature range
kpis: Cold-chain shipments with a continuous temperature log
Temperature excursion alerts acknowledged
within 30 minutes
Goods with an excursion released without a quality decision
beliefs: Vaccines and insulin need 2 to 8 degrees Celsius
constraints: Only the Quality Assurance Officer may release goods after an excursion

elements.text: Stream readings from the shipment's temperature data logger to the cold-chain monitoring service continuously from pick-up to hospital hand-over
Scan each cold-chain handover (loading, transfer, hospital receipt) so the temperature log has no unmonitored gap
Raise an excursion alert to the Responsible Pharmacist and the Quality Assurance Officer when a reading leaves the 2 to 8 degrees Celsius range
Require explicit acknowledgement of each excursion alert and escalate to the Quality Assurance Officer's deputy if it is not acknowledged within the agreed response time
Quarantine the affected batches automatically on excursion and keep them blocked until a quality decision is recorded
Block dispatch and delivery-note printing in the order portal for any order line linked to a quarantined batch
Record the Quality Assurance Officer's release or rejection decision with identity, timestamp, temperature evidence and reason in an audit trail
Report to the Hospital Buyer any shipment delayed or rejected because of an excursion, with the replacement plan
Temperature data loggers in every cold-chain shipper and in the cold rooms
Cold-chain monitoring dashboard with excursion alert and acknowledgement queue
Stock and batch module holding batch, expiry, storage class and quarantine status
Quality Assurance Officer
Responsible Pharmacist
Sales Administrator
Hospital Buyer
Vaccines and insulin must be kept between 2 and 8 degrees Celsius
Loggers record at a fixed short interval (every five minutes), so a missing interval counts as a gap in the log
Only the Quality Assurance Officer may release goods after a temperature excursion
Goods with an unresolved excursion cannot be picked, dispatched or invoiced
A cold-chain shipment may not leave the warehouse without an active logger paired to its shipment record

sub_goals.text: Access to order, stock, and contract data verified for every request (zero trust)
kpis: Requests authenticated and authorized per request
Privileged actions protected by multi-factor authentication
Quarterly access reviews completed
beliefs: No network location, including the office network, is trusted by default

elements.text: LLM ordering assistant requests verified under the named end user's delegated identity
Authenticate every request to the order portal and to the ordering assistant against the corporate identity provider
Evaluate access policy per request (role, device, context, customer contract scope) before order, stock or contract data is released
Cache policy decisions for 5 minutes for non-privileged read requests while re-verifying every privileged action
Require step-up multi-factor authentication for privileged actions (contract price changes, bulk data export, quarantine release, access rights changes)
Review all user, service and assistant access rights per role every quarter and revoke rights that are no longer justified
Record each access review and each revocation in the access review register and close it within the quarter
Issue the ordering assistant a short-lived credential bound to the named hospital buyer or sales administrator for each session, never a standing service identity
Log every verified request with user identity, assistant session, and the order, batch or contract record accessed

The LLM ordering assistant is a requester like any other and is never implicitly trusted
Shared accounts are not permitted, for human users and for the ordering assistant
Cached authorization decisions may not be used for privileged actions

sub_goals.text: Personal data of hospital staff and named patients protected
kpis: Personal data fields classified with a documented purpose
Patient identifiers stored outside named-patient order records
Data subject requests closed
within the legal deadline
beliefs: Named-patient orders contain a patient name and medical record number
constraints: Patient identifiers are not sent to the language model provider

elements.text: Maintain a data inventory recording, for every personal data field of hospital staff and named patients in the order portal and the ordering assistant, its purpose, legal basis and retention period
Classify each personal data field as staff contact data or patient identifier and flag fields without a documented purpose for deletion or purpose assignment
Scan portal databases, exports, reports and log files for patient names and medical record numbers outside named-patient order records and remove or relocate the findings
Mask or pseudonymise patient identifiers and staff personal data in test, training and analytics environments
Filter patient identifiers out of prompts, retrieval context and logs of the LLM-based ordering assistant before any call to the model provider
Register and verify the identity of each data subject request from hospital staff or patients and record its legal deadline
Export, correct or erase the requester's personal data across the portal, the assistant stores and backups, and close the request within the legal deadline
Personal data inventory of the order portal and the ordering assistant

Data subject request register with verification evidence and deadline tracking

sub_goals.text: Ordering assistant governed as an AI system
kpis: Assistant answers that cite an approved source
Hospital-specific prices disclosed to another hospital in the monthly audit
Answers rated correct in the monthly evaluation
Model and prompt changes approved before release
beliefs: The assistant runs on an external model provider
constraints: The assistant cannot place or change an order without the buyer's confirmation
Patient identifiers are not sent to the language model provider

elements.text: Assistant answers grounded in the approved pharmaceutical corpus and traceable to a cited source
Hospital-specific commercial and patient data kept confidential in assistant interactions
Model and prompt changes and AI risks governed under approval and review
Retrieve assistant answers only from the approved product, contract and regulatory corpus and attach the source citation to every answer
Escalate out-of-scope, clinical or product-quality questions to the Responsible Pharmacist or Sales Administrator instead of answering
Run a monthly evaluation of the assistant on a fixed test set of hospital ordering questions and record the correctness rating of each answer
Hold or block assistant answers that fail the source-citation check and route them for human review before they reach the hospital buyer
Keep a register of every model version and prompt change with requester, approver and release date
Approve each model or prompt change in the register before release and re-run the evaluation test set after release
Review the AI risk assessment of the ordering assistant with the Quality Assurance Officer, the IT Security Officer and the Data Protection Officer on a fixed periodic basis
Filter retrieval and answer generation by the buyer's hospital entitlement so that only that hospital's contract prices and order history can be used
Audit the monthly sample of assistant interaction logs for disclosure of another hospital's prices or contract terms
Present the assistant's proposed order lines to the hospital buyer for explicit confirmation in the order portal before any order is created or changed
